$comment: The register of every eval suite TEA can run, and of every skill it has agreed not to cover yet.
`npm run eval:all` discovers its suites here and refuses to run when a TEA skill appears in neither list.
That refusal is the point: a suite list with a skill missing from it reads as coverage, and reading it that
way is the most expensive possible mistake to make about your own quality gate.
Only `evalType: behavioral` discharges a skill's coverage obligation. Fragment selection measures which
knowledge a run loads, which is a routing decision taken before the workflow produces anything, so none of the
eight skills it spans is still listed under `deferred`. All eight, `atdd`, `automate`, `ci`, `framework`, `nfr`,
`test-design`, `test-review` and `trace`, each carry a behavioral suite of their own, and that is what
discharges them.
`ciTier` is the tier at which a suite runs in full. `npm run eval:all -- --preflight-only` runs each suite's
`harnessOptions.preflightArgs` instead, which validates the data and then probes the runner: the executable
answers --version and a built-in vendor has a credential. No model call is made. tools/validate-eval-schemas.js
drives that argv once with a missing runner and once with a present one, so a preflight that never reaches the
runner fails `npm test`. The deterministic pull-request tier runs the data half alone, through --validate-only.
Thresholds are declared here and checked against the harness constants by tools/validate-eval-schemas.js.
Editing one side alone fails `npm test`, so the manifest cannot drift into describing a gate that is not the
gate being run. `caseCount` is checked the same way, against the case-id list each harness exports, and
`runnerCapabilities` against the RUNNER_CAPABILITIES each harness exports and hands to its runner.
`contracts` names the eval contracts under test/contracts/ that express a suite. The same check fails when a
listed path is missing and when a generated contract is claimed by no suite, so the link cannot rot in either
direction. It is an array because a suite can need more than one: `bmad-tea-routing` is eighteen intents and
eval-quality's AD-39 scripting bound caps an interaction plan at sixteen steps, so its corpus is expressed as
an intents contract and a controls contract. test/contracts/README.md records the split.
`bmad-teach-me-testing` ships no knowledge index at all, so fragment selection does not apply to it; its own
behavioral suite, `teach-me-testing`, is what discharges it.
One story, quay-locker-service, staged into a disposable workspace and generated against by a
vendor run, then executed under NFR9's isolation by the deterministic tea-atdd-red-check, which
spends no vendor call of its own.
Five acceptance criteria, four asking for a route the fixture does not have and one extending a
route it already has, which is what makes a vacuous pass possible: a scaffold that asserts only
what the fixture already returns passes with no implementation at all. A test maps to a criterion
by carrying its id, AC-<n>, in its title, the workflow's own scaffold convention.
redForIntendedReasonRate is 1 and every other way of not being red for the intended reason carries
its own zero ceiling beside it: a vacuous pass, a scaffold left skipped after activation, a spec
file that never parsed, a failure that does not match the criterion's declared message pattern,
and a test naming no criterion. Nothing here admits slack, because AC1's own rule is a binary
classification with no defensible middle case at this corpus size.
runnerCapabilities names only the generation half. Execution spends no vendor call and is not a
runner capability in this vocabulary, so it is confined by cli/lib/atdd-isolation.js instead, proven
by test/test-atdd-isolation.js before this suite is registered.
No live agent and no generation step, unlike every other suite here. Four hand-authored Playwright spec
sets under test/fixtures/automate-eval/cases/ stand in for what a real bmad-testarch-automate run could
produce against the Story 6.6 voucher-service fixture, and every one of them actually runs, twice: once
against the fixed implementation and once against a scratch copy carrying the fixture's seeded
regression (the minimum-spend boundary flipped from inclusive to exclusive).
correct-run tests the boundary itself and is the only case whose mutated run must fail, with the failure
attributed to the seeded boundary through a declared message pattern. The other three each stand in for a
different way generated coverage can look thorough and catch nothing: misses-regression asserts only
interior values and passes on both runs, vacuous-pass asserts something that cannot fail against real
behavior, and duplicate repeats one assertion under a second title. All three must be reported as such
rather than as a clean pass, which is what every threshold below ceilings at zero: on this exact,
hand-authored corpus the scorer has to classify all four cases correctly, every time.
runnerCapabilities names command-execution rather than scoped-artifact-writes: this harness spawns
Playwright and the fixture's own server as child processes and reads their output back, and writes
nothing else. `--agent` / `--agent-cmd` are accepted only so this harness's argv matches every other
suite's for tools/validate-eval-schemas.js's preflight-probe check; the harness's own header explains why
no live-agent mode exists to select between.
contracts is empty, which the schema allows for a suite with no contract yet: eval-quality's oracle
vocabulary can only address evidence a real interaction produced, and test/test-probe-targets.js's
registry check refuses any contract naming a CLI interface this repository does not actually ship (the
exact mistake it exists to catch, once made for months by eight contracts naming a runner that did not
exist). This suite ships no command at all, so there is no real interaction for a contract to address; a
fictional `tea-automate-runner` interface would satisfy the schema and fail that registry check the same
way the runner it once caught did. `atdd.contract.json` is the nearest precedent for the same limit: its
oracles already stop at the one real command atdd ships and never address `cli/atdd-red-check.js`'s
deterministic half, because that half is not a vendor-calling interaction either.
18 intents put to `bmad-tea`, one agent call each: ten with one right menu item, four where two or more
items are genuinely close and the right answer is to ask, and four nothing on the menu serves.
`fixtures` is the intent corpus, which is the only file the agent is shown. `groundTruth` is the oracle,
and the harness searches every assembled prompt for its keys and its bytes before it spends a call, so the
separation is asserted rather than assumed.
Three of the nine thresholds are the controls and they close the cells recall leaves open. Recall alone rewards
a system that routes everything, and the two `maxConfidentRoutesOn...` counts refuse that on both the
unservable and the genuinely close intents; a system that asks about everything never routes wrong, and
`maxUnroutedClearIntents` refuses that.
Two repetitions. Each case is one short reply rather than a whole workflow, so the cost is low, and two is
the smallest number that can say whether a routing decision is reproducible.
24 cases across the eight workflow skills that ship a knowledge index. The case data and the expectation
live in the same file, so `fixtures` and `groundTruth` name the same paths on purpose: the oracle here was
quoted from each workflow's own step files rather than written independently of the case.
Two projects, two written requests, each its own service and each its own thresholds.
`fixtures` is the two projects plus their request files. `groundTruth` is the oracle, which the
harness searches every assembled prompt and every staged file for before it spends a call, the
same guard every sibling suite applies.
Two thresholds are the point of the suite and both are zero: a generated workflow must parse and
must lint clean under actionlint, pinned flags recorded in every result record. The recall over
requested elements and the accuracy over triggers alone carry the judgment about whether the run
read the request; the unrequested-element ceiling and the two workflow-rule ceilings close the
cells recall leaves open, the way bmad-tea-routing's three counts close cells its own recall leaves
open: a run that copies the shipped template regardless of what was asked would still keep every
requested element and score well on recall alone.
Two repetitions. A full CI scaffold reads four step files, a template and several knowledge
fragments, and writes a workflow plus helper scripts and documentation, so it costs more than a
fragment selection, and two is the smallest number that can say whether the answer is reproducible.
Two evidence bundles, each its own set of thresholds, each audited in its own staged workspace.
Combining them would judge one service's measurement against another service's target, which is
why they are never one run.
`fixtures` lists every file the agent is given and `groundTruth` names the file it must never see.
The harness asserts that separation on the staged workspace and on the prompt before it spends a call.
`caseCount` is 2: one case per bundle, which is one staged workspace and one agent call. The
fourteen fixture files are the inputs those two cases read, and the harness exports the case ids so
tools/validate-eval-schemas.js checks this number against the list the run actually scores.
The headline is `maxUnsupportedPass` at 0. The gapped bundle carries two domains the workflow's own
rules say cannot reach a PASS on the evidence it holds, and the clean bundle carries four that can,
so a workflow that never passes anything fails this suite as surely as one that passes everything.
Two fixture sets, each one epic document and each its own case, so one staged workspace and one
agent call apiece. They are never designed in one run: combining them changes every ratio, and the
clean set exists so recall cannot be met by reporting everything.
`fixtures` lists the two epics the agent is given and `groundTruth` names the file it must never
see. The harness asserts that separation on the staged workspace and on the prompt before it spends
a call, and --validate-only asserts it too, so the check does not only run when a model runs.
The runner needs a scoped write because the workflow's deliverable is a document it must create.
Two repetitions. A full epic-level design reads five step files, the epic and several knowledge
fragments, so it costs far more than a fragment selection, and two is the smallest number that can
say whether the answer is reproducible.
READ THIS BEFORE TREATING THIS SUITE'S CONTRACT AS COVERAGE.
The thresholds above are the harness's, and the harness is the only thing that checks them. The
contract this suite links is deliberately weaker than the harness, because the workflow declares
one output and it is prose: `{test_artifacts}/test-design-epic-{epic_num}.md`, with nothing
machine-readable beside it. bmad-testarch-trace writes e2e-trace-summary.json next to its markdown
matrix, which is how the trace contract states the matrix's content through arithmetic its oracles
can reach. Test-design has no summary to point at, so every oracle here addresses the document as a
whole and can only ask which vocabulary it carries. The arithmetic, the band placement, the
coverage mapping and the priority ordering are checked by the harness, and by the eleven stored
documents under test/replay/test-design/ that re-derive all four through test/test-eval-replay.js
in `npm test` with no model call. No oracle in this contract reaches any of the four.
So a green test/test-contract-oracles.js says the contract and the harness agree about the
vocabulary. It is not this suite passing, and it is not a substitute for running it. Closing that
gap needs the workflow to emit a machine-readable summary of its register and coverage plan. That
gap is reported here and carries no story yet, and it is not work this suite can do from the
consumer side.
One review call covers all three fixtures, so the three case ids share the prompt bundle digest.
The runner needs a scoped write because the workflow's deliverable is a report file it must create.
Two fixture sets, each its own coverage oracle with its own gate decision, each traced in its own
staged workspace. Combining them changes every percentage, which is why they are never one run.
`fixtures` lists every file the agent is given and `groundTruth` names the file it must never see.
The harness asserts that separation on the staged workspace and on the prompt before it spends a call.
`caseCount` is 2: one case per fixture set, which is one staged workspace and one agent call. The
fourteen fixture files are the inputs those two cases read, and the harness exports the case ids so
tools/validate-eval-schemas.js checks this number against the list the run actually scores.
Two repetitions. A full trace is a five-step run over a whole project tree, so it costs far more than a
fragment selection, and two is the smallest number that can say whether the answer is reproducible.
evalType: infrastructure, not behavioral: this suite proves the reusable multi-turn
transcript-driving engine, test/lib/transcript-harness.js's runTranscript, against a trivial
scripted three-turn session. It discharges no skill's coverage obligation and declares neither
skill nor skills, the same way fragment-selection's evalType already withholds coverage while
measuring something real. bmad-teach-me-testing stays in deferred until Story 6.11 actually
measures it with this engine; this suite proving the engine works is not that measurement.
The one registered case always drives test/fixtures/transcript-runner/stub-agent.js through
--agent custom --agent-cmd, hardcoded by the suite regardless of the --agent flag eval:all was
given, so it spends no vendor call and is fully reproducible: ciTier deterministic fits for the
same reason it fits atdd's isolation proof and no other behavioral suite here, no credential, no
model spend, runs on every PR.
contracts is deliberately empty. No eval-quality contract, oracle, or probe-corpus machinery
backs this suite; test/contracts/README.md's discipline is for a suite that states a skill's
behavior in that vocabulary, and this one proves a harness mechanism in plain assertions instead,
test/test-transcript-harness.js's own contradictory-script and mid-session-failure proofs among
them. The one threshold is named on the cross-turn check: crossTurnConsistencyRate is the
property a multi-turn session exists to prove can be checked at all.
Why this doesn't fit the existing agent-eval shape cleanly, and why it's registered in suites[] anyway: all
other behavioral suites here invoke a live agent and score what it produced. bmad-testarch-framework's
'generation' step is a parameterized template copy, not a live-agent judgment call -- Story 6.8 already
scored the committed fixture's contents statically with zero agent involvement. This suite is 100%
execution and 0% generation: it copies the committed clean fixture into a disposable workspace, runs a real
`npm install` and a real smoke test (tests/e2e/api-sample.spec.ts only -- ui-sample.spec.ts needs a real
Chromium navigation and stays out of scope) against a minimal in-memory stub backend, inside NFR9 isolation
extended with one loopback-bound CONNECT-allowlisting proxy that permits exactly one external host
(registry.npmjs.org) and nothing else. No vendor call is ever made; runnerCapabilities describes this
harness's OWN sandboxed execution step, the same generic vocabulary ATDD's own execution half is confined
by rather than a stretch of it, since the schema documents it as a policy declaration and not narrowly as a
live agent's own permission. `--agent` is accepted only for eval:all's CLI uniformity and is never read.
`groundTruth` names the same file as `fixtures` on purpose: the sample spec's own assertions are the
oracle here, which the schema's own comment anticipates ("a suite whose oracle is also its input has to
say so rather than let a reader assume the two were written independently").
`repetitions` is 1: a deterministic install-and-run against a fixed fixture has no stochastic process to
average over, unlike every other suite's repetition count, which exists to average over LLM stochasticity.
`seededDefectDetectionRate` is the second threshold, measured only once `installAndSmokePassRate` already
passed: a backend seeded to answer the wrong status and a workspace copy seeded to drop its own auth fixture
from mergeTests(...) must each fail the smoke test for its own distinct, verified reason. A suite whose
smoke test cannot be observed to fail is decorative regardless of how often it passes; this threshold is
what rules that out on every live run, not only once by hand.
The suite that retires bmad-teach-me-testing from deferred, reusing Story 6.10's transcript-driving
engine and runner completely unchanged: one case, two turns, against a real vendor. Turn 1 plays the
whole first-session path through the real skill, itself supplying both the facilitator (following the
real step files exactly) and a scripted learner (role, Beginner experience, learning goals, session
1, a deliberately wrong answer to session-1's own Q1, the resulting below-70% [R] review choice, and
exit). Turn 2 is a brand-new, memoryless process in the same persistent workspace that proves progress
persistence is real rather than assumed: a headless agent CLI carries no session state between
invocations, so a fresh process correctly finding and reporting progress.yaml is the only thing that
actually proves the file, not the model's own context, is what carries state forward.
Every check is a mechanical containment or equality test over structural data -- does progress.yaml's
experience_level equal the fixture's declared level, does turn 1's transcript contain the step file's
own verbatim correction text for the seeded wrong answer, does that same corrective content reappear
AFTER the [R] review choice (not merely once, from the original mistake), does turn 2 land on the
continuation greeting rather than the fresh-start one, and does every session progress.yaml claims
`completed` correspond to a session the transcript actually shows was quizzed -- never a semantic
judgment of reply quality. test/test-teach-me-testing-scoring.js proves each of the four scoring
functions this suite shares with the story spec (placementHolds, correctionHolds, reTeachingHolds,
masteryClaimHolds) actually fails on a hand-built violation before this suite is trusted to run one.
AC2 was rewritten before this suite was built: bmad-teach-me-testing has no mechanism, in any
session, where a wrong answer on one topic pulls in a different topic the pre-correction plan did not
already have (see _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/epics.md's Story 6.11 finding). The real branch is
[R] review the same session's content again, or [C] continue anyway, and reTeachingHolds scores that
real branch instead.
contracts is deliberately empty, the same declared deviation test/eval-transcript.js records for its
own reason: every check here is the same containment/equality shape test/eval-atdd.js's scoreRun
already uses for comparably structural claims, and test/test-teach-me-testing-scoring.js's own
pure-function proof is what gives that shape independent verification without a contract adding
value the proof does not already give.
One repetition by default: this is a live-cost suite spending two real vendor calls (one per turn),
not the free scripted exchange test/eval-transcript.js proves the engine against, so
ciTier full-matrix matches nfr's, ci's, and atdd's own live suites rather than transcript's
deterministic tier.
